correction: Token wrote a sender's name unquoted unless it held , ; or a quote, and an address as it came, so a name with a line break (or an address whose quoted local part held a comma) read back as an extra recipient in a reply. Token now turns control characters into spaces, drops quotes, quotes any name with RFC 5322 specials, and quotes an address it cannot write plainly as one invalid piece; addresses with white space, controls or , ; " < > are no longer valid.
